summary:
I've been building a Japanese-learning app for myself, Keikochō, and the interesting problem right now isn't the app, it's the curriculum. I measured what my own conversational practice mode was actually doing and found that across a set of personas, one answer covers something like 75-100% of the questions — the content varied on paper but the right answer was predictable enough that there was nothing to actually listen for. That's now driving a rebuild of how the bot's "personality" works: instead of hand-authored opinions per topic, it's a small rule keyed to word categories, so an LLM authors the character offline and the deterministic runtime never has to touch it live.

I also picked up an odd one: giving fourteen chat personas fourteen distinct voices instead of two recycled ones. The catch was that the TTS engine I wanted for variety has no way to ask "what will you actually say" before it speaks — the engine I'd been using rejects a bad pronunciation before any audio exists, which is how I catch the app mispronouncing things. So the new voices are scoped to conversation practice only, never to anything the learner is asked to read back, which is the one place a silent mispronunciation would actually teach the wrong thing.

On the infra side, I run a small home lab and had a GPU-serialization proxy that was supposed to auto-restart on reboot silently sit dead for an hour after a routine restart, because Docker treats "explicitly stopped" as sticky across reboots even with a restart policy that's supposed to bring it back. Nothing paged, which is the actual bug — a monitor that can fail quietly is worse than no monitor. Fixed it and then spent some time auditing the rest of that fleet for the same pattern, which turned up a couple more services that had been down for weeks without anyone noticing.

Also did a pass on a client-facing D&D companion app's video calling, where a "nobody can hear each other" bug turned out to be a one-line miss: the client subscribed to remote audio tracks but never actually attached them to a playable element, so every browser connected and saw each other fine and just... didn't play sound. Wrote a two-browser headless test harness to prove the fix actually carries audio end to end before shipping it, rather than trusting that "no errors in the console" meant it worked.

highlights.oneLiner: Measuring おしゃべり persona answer predictability, redesigning personality as a sem-keyed rule
Giving 14 chat personas 14 distinct voices, scoped away from anything the learner reads aloud
Fixed a GPU-serialization proxy that silently stayed dead after a reboot, audited the fleet for the same pattern
Fixed a video call audio bug (subscribed but never attached) with a two-browser headless test harness
